title: Ear protection: plugs and muffs
summary: Why a shot can damage hearing for good, which plugs and muffs exist, and why many Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters wear both on loud ranges.

body.html: Hearing protection is compulsory in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting for everyone on or near a layout: shooters, referees, staff and spectators. A shooter who comes to the stand without it is treated as absent and does not shoot.

A shotgun shot is very loud: about 160–170 dB at the shooter's ear at its loudest instant. For short, sudden noises like a bang (impulse noise) the usual safe limit is 140 dB for adults and 120 dB for children. So each shot without protection is over the limit, and a day at the ground means hundreds of shots, yours and other people's.

Noise-induced hearing loss builds up gradually and without pain. Tiny sensitive cells in the inner ear die, and they do not grow back. It usually starts with high sounds: speech, especially in a noisy place, becomes less clear, and many people do not notice it at first. With further unprotected shooting the loss spreads to more sounds. Lost hearing cannot be restored; it can only be protected.

Ringing or buzzing in the ears (tinnitus) after shooting is a common first warning: your protection was not enough. Check how your plugs and muffs fit, or choose stronger ones. If your ears ring or sounds seem muffled after shooting, have your hearing tested by an ear, nose and throat doctor or an audiologist. If your hearing drops suddenly, get medical help urgently.

Earplugs are the simplest option. Foam plugs are cheap: you roll them thin, insert them into the ear and let them expand. There are also reusable silicone plugs and custom plugs moulded to your ear. Plugs that seal the ear canal protect well; badly fitted ones protect very little, so ask your coach to show you.

Passive ear muffs simply cover the ears with tight cups. They are easy to put on and take off, but voices are harder to hear through them. For a shotgun choose muffs with slim cups, because thick ones can hit the stock as you mount the gun.

Electronic ear muffs have microphones and speakers. They amplify quiet sounds, such as the referee's voice and commands, and cut a loud sound instantly at the moment of the shot. They help safety and communication, but they cost more and need batteries or charging.

Protection is rated with a number, SNR in Europe and NRR in the USA: the higher the number, the stronger the reduction. On loud ranges, such as under a roof or near walls, plugs and muffs worn together give an extra margin. You cannot simply add the two numbers together, but a US workplace-safety institute (NIOSH) measured roughly 15–20 dB more protection with both than with one alone.

Protection works only when it fits well. Plugs go in deep enough to seal the ear canal, and glasses arms or a hat must not break the seal of the muffs. Custom plugs are comfortable and fit the same way each time; use the SNR on the pack as a guide.

For children and juniors hearing protection matters even more: their ears are damaged more easily, so the safe noise limit for children is set lower than for adults (140 dB for adults and 120 dB for children).
Many coaches suggest plugs and muffs together for children. Put protection on before you walk up to the stand, and keep it on while anyone nearby is shooting.

notes.html: Electronic muffs let you hear the coach and the referee while your hearing stays protected. Many interpreters find them a good choice for long days on the stand.

key_points.html: Hearing protection is compulsory for everyone near the stand.
A shot is about 160–170 dB at the shooter's ear at its loudest instant; noise damage adds up and does not heal.
Plugs protect only when they seal the ear canal.
Ringing ears after shooting mean the protection was not enough.
On loud ranges plugs and muffs together give extra protection; many coaches suggest both for children.

did_you_know.html: Foam earplugs are meant for one or a few uses: worn and dirty plugs seal less well and protect less.

quiz.q: What do electronic ear muffs do?

options.text: Amplify quiet sounds and cut the shot
Count how many shots you have fired
Replace the need for safety glasses

quiz.explain: You hear the referee and commands while your hearing is protected.

quiz.q: Why are slim-cup muffs better for a shotgun?

options.text: They let more of the bang through
Thick cups can hit the stock
The dress code asks for slim cups
They need no batteries at all

quiz.explain: The stock comes up to the cheek, and a thick cup can get in the way of the mount.

quiz.q: What is sensible on a very loud stand, for example under a roof?

options.text: Wear just one of the earplugs
Stand closer to the trap house

quiz.explain: Double protection reduces sound more than either one alone.
